gloss: to top up; to add more; to replenish

definitions.gloss: to top up; to add more; to replenish
definitions.explanation: To pour or add more of a liquid or substance to something that is running low.

examples.japanese: お{湯|ゆ}を{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}した。
examples.english: I topped up the hot water.

examples.japanese: グラスが{空|から}になりかけたので、ワインを{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}した。
examples.english: The glass was almost empty, so I poured more wine.

examples.japanese: スープが{少|すく}なくなってきたら、{水|みず}を{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}しながら{煮込|にこ}んでください。
examples.english: If the soup starts running low, simmer it while adding more water.

notes:
A compound verb combining {注|つ}ぐ (to pour) and {足|た}す (to add, supplement). Specifically describes the action of replenishing a liquid or substance that has been partially consumed or reduced. Very common in cooking and dining contexts.

USAGE:
- Primarily used for liquids: water, soup, oil, beverages
- Implies the container already has some of the substance — you are adding more
- In Japanese dining culture, it is polite to {注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す drinks for others before they run out

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive (takes を)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{湯|ゆ}を{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to top up hot water
- {水|みず}を{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to add more water
- {油|あぶら}を{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to top up the oil
- ビールを{注|つ}ぎ{足|た}す: to pour more beer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {足|た}す: to add — more general; not limited to pouring
- {注|つ}ぐ: to pour — the base verb; simply pouring, not specifically replenishing
- {補充|ほじゅう}する: to replenish, restock — more formal; used for supplies and inventory
- おかわりする: to have another serving — from the recipient's perspective; asking for more
